overview: Both are protein-digesting enzymes, but they're secreted in different organs and work best at very different pH levels.
genZNote: Pepsin: works in the stomach's acid bath. Trypsin: works in the intestine's alkaline environment.

aspects.label: Site of Secretion/Action
aspects.valueA: Secreted by gastric glands, acts in the stomach.
aspects.valueB: Secreted by the pancreas, acts in the small intestine.

aspects.label: Activated From
aspects.valueA: Activated from inactive pepsinogen by stomach acid (HCl).
aspects.valueB: Activated from inactive trypsinogen by the enzyme enterokinase.

aspects.label: Acts On
aspects.valueB: Breaks proteins/polypeptides into smaller peptides and amino acids.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both enzymes are secreted as inactive precursors (zymogens) — pepsinogen and trypsinogen — to protect the secreting tissue from self-digestion.
overlay.memoryTrick: Pepsin = stomach, acidic. Trypsin = intestine, alkaline (pancreatic).
overlay.commonMisconception: Trypsin would actually be destroyed by stomach acid — its alkaline-optimum design is exactly why protein digestion continues in the intestine rather than in the acidic stomach.
